generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The addition of `@SuppressForbidden` indicates that setting system properties is being suppressed for security reasons. Ensure that this is necessary and does not introduce vulnerabilities. The reason provided should be reviewed to confirm it accurately reflects the necessity.

Changing `platformLibDir` from private to public in `LoaderHelper` makes it accessible outside the class. This could lead to unintended modifications if other parts of the codebase access and modify this field directly. Consider whether making this field public is necessary or if a getter method would suffice.

Introducing a static block to set the JNA library path in `JnaNativeLibraryProvider` ensures that the path is set before any instances of the class are created. However, this approach assumes that no other code will attempt to load libraries before this static block executes. Consider potential concurrency issues if multiple threads could initialize this class simultaneously.

The method `setJnaLibraryPath` sets a system property which affects the behavior of JNA library loading globally. This can have unintended side effects if other parts of the application or third-party libraries rely on JNA and expect different settings. Ensure that this change does not interfere with other components.

review_comment: Would it be better to do this in `SystemJvmOptions` rather than in a static initializer?

No, that was the problem we had before, it made NativeAccess unusable in the CLI. I moved it into here so that this can work even when we haven't gone through SystemJvmOptions (which is only for the main ES process).

review_comment: Will `toString` return a path with the right separators to be parsed properly on all platforms?

Yes. The javadoc for `Path.toString()` mentions the following:

> The returned path string uses the default name separator to separate names in the path.
Sounds good. I wasn't totally certain the "default name separator" was one that worked on all platforms.
